These compounds are all known to interact with the same target, indicating a possible common pathway or mechanism of action. The integration of these pathways suggests that 3'-Methoxyglabridin may exert its effects through a similar mechanism, possibly by modulating the activity of the voltage-dependent T-type calcium channel subunit alpha-1I, which in turn influences the function of the high affinity cationic amino acid transporter 1. The evidence points to a possible dependency on the activity of this channel, highlighting a potential role for 3'-Methoxyglabridin in modulating transporter function through a shared target.
